ctx.x: that place, man, and they took up half the room. The band took up almost -- those rooms, you got to remember, they never did seat over 75, 80, 85 people, hardly any of those rooms in there, because about a 14 piece band in there, you know, it's some guy -- the piano was down on the floor. You had to have that down there, and you had all the guys -- I guess that's why they sounded good. They all were concentrated right together, like up in a little nook or something like that. And they sounded real good.

Mildred Bailey was on 52nd Street then, and at Kelly's Stables -- I remember once at Kelly's Stables Coleman Hawkins was in there; Billy Daniels -- all at the same time -- Billy Daniels was in there; Nat Cole trio was in there. And who else was in there? Some singer -- I can't think who was in, some girl.
But all of them were in there, and another thing, I don't think any of them made over about 100 bucks a week, and all of them were in that -- in Kelly's Stables that one time.
